tracker_name: Democracy Risk and Institutional Resilience Tracker
_schema_note: Append one object to `weeks` per run. Never edit or delete a past entry's original scores — see protocol.md Section 21. To correct a past week, add a `retrospective_revision` object to that week's entry instead.

indicators.name: Media retaliation
indicators.note: DOJ subpoenas to at least four NYT reporters and their relatives, some served at home by federal agents, in a leak probe over Air Force One safety reporting; press-freedom groups call it an unprecedented escalation.

indicators.name: Agency weaponization
indicators.note: OPM finalized a rule centralizing and expanding grounds to fire career civil servants, alongside a continuing pattern of DOJ action against perceived opponents.

indicators.name: Narrative warfare
indicators.note: President revived unsubstantiated election-fraud claims in a White House speech, including an uncorroborated claim that China compromised 220 million voter files.

indicators.name: Corruption/impunity
indicators.note: A federal judge voided a Trump/IRS settlement as bad-faith self-dealing with 'no basis in law,' surfacing the underlying attempt even as the court blocked it.

indicators.name: State-level conflict
indicators.note: National Guard deployments in Washington, D.C. remain a flashpoint with Democratic governors, continuing tension from prior weeks.

indicators.name: Election manipulation
indicators.note: New Hampshire's secretary of state confirmed federal election monitors will be deployed to some primary polling places; deployment not yet implemented.

indicators.name: Judiciary attacks
indicators.note: No new intimidation event this week; baseline risk continues from earlier threats against judges who ruled against the administration.

indicators.name: Judicial independence
indicators.note: Courts issued multiple substantive rulings against the administration this week (IRS settlement voided, grant terminations blocked) with no evidence of defiance.

indicators.name: State-level resistance
indicators.note: A 24-state coalition won final summary judgment over illegal grant terminations; Connecticut won dismissal of a DOJ demand for its voter rolls; secretaries of state met to prepare for anticipated federal interference.

indicators.name: Election-administration integrity
indicators.note: Officials preserved control of voter data in Connecticut, but confirmed federal monitor deployment to New Hampshire polling places raises independence concerns.

indicators.name: Media and watchdog capacity
indicators.note: Outlets continued reporting on self-dealing and pardons despite subpoena pressure; press-freedom organizations and lawmakers spoke out, though a chilling effect is evident.

indicators.name: Civil-service independence
indicators.note: New OPM rule expands grounds and centralizes authority to fire career employees, continuing erosion of merit-system protections.

indicators.name: Legislative oversight
indicators.note: A Senate resolution condemning DOJ subpoenas of journalists was filed, but it is symbolic and non-binding with no enforcement mechanism.

indicators.name: Accountability enforcement
indicators.note: Courts delivered real consequences this week: a voided settlement, blocked grant cuts, and a dismissed federal lawsuit against a state.

weeks.relationship_note: Pressure remains elevated across media, agency, and narrative fronts, but courts and states delivered a string of enforced, favorable-to-democracy outcomes this week that kept the gap from widening.

event_log.actor: U.S. District Judge Kathleen Williams (S.D. Fla.)
event_log.action: Voided an IRS settlement purporting to immunize Trump and family/business interests from audits over past filings, calling it a bad-faith attempt to manipulate the judicial process with 'no basis in law,' and barred the administration from citing it in future proceedings.
event_log.notes: Underlying settlement attempt reveals self-dealing motive, but the court's intervention is a strong, enforced check rather than a mere statement of concern.

event_log.target: At least four New York Times reporters and their family members
event_log.action: Issued third-party subpoenas for reporters' and relatives' phone/text records, some served by federal agents at reporters' homes, compelling grand jury testimony in Manhattan as part of a leak investigation into Air Force One safety reporting.
event_log.notes: Committee to Protect Journalists calls it an 'extraordinary escalation'; part of a pattern of at least three prior journalist-subpoena episodes in recent months.

event_log.target: Career federal civil servants (est. tens of thousands)
event_log.action: Finalized a rule centralizing and expanding grounds to fire federal employees (e.g., late tax filing, NDA violations, 'unsuitability'), reducing appeal rights as part of the Schedule Policy/Career rollout.
event_log.notes: AFGE and other unions call this a further erosion of merit-based protections, following June's Schedule F expansion to roughly 8,000 positions.

event_log.actor: U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani (D. Mass.)
event_log.target: Trump administration OMB; 24-state coalition of plaintiffs
event_log.action: Granted summary judgment to a 24-state coalition, ruling the administration illegally used a budget-office regulation to terminate congressionally-approved federal grants.
event_log.notes: Final judgment, not a preliminary injunction — a strong demonstration that spending-power constraints on the executive are being enforced.

event_log.actor: U.S. District Judge Kari A. Dooley
event_log.action: Dismissed a DOJ lawsuit seeking Connecticut's full statewide voter registration list, ruling DOJ has no authority under the Civil Rights Act of 1960 to compel its production.
event_log.notes: One of several state wins this week rebuffing DOJ voter-data demands; preserves state control over election records.

event_log.action: In a White House speech, revived unsubstantiated election-fraud claims, including an unsupported allegation that China compromised 220 million U.S. voter files, without presenting new evidence.
event_log.notes: A Senate Intelligence Committee vice chair publicly disputed the claims; continues a pattern dating to 2020 of unsubstantiated fraud allegations.

event_log.actor: State secretaries of state (NASS summer conference)
event_log.target: Anticipated federal interference with election administration
event_log.action: States including Minnesota discussed proactively 'gaming out' scenarios for federal interference and began backfilling election-administration services previously provided by the federal government.
event_log.notes: Proactive rather than reactive resilience — states positioning ahead of anticipated pressure rather than responding to an implemented action.

event_log.action: New Hampshire's Republican secretary of state confirmed the state had been told federal election monitors will be deployed to some polling places during upcoming primaries.
event_log.notes: Confirmed by a Republican official, not disputed; monitors not yet deployed as of report, so operational effect is unconfirmed.

event_log.actor: Sen. Alex Padilla and Senate Democrats
event_log.action: Sounded alarm on DOJ threats to journalists and joined a resolution condemning administration attacks on the free press.
event_log.notes: Per protocol Section 4.4, a non-binding resolution is weak evidence of resilience — noted but not treated as a strong constraint.

weeks.trajectory_note: This is the first tracked week, so no 90-day trend line yet exists. The baseline picture combines severe, sustained pressure — DOJ subpoenas reaching journalists' families, an OPM rule further stripping civil-service job protections, and a presidential speech reviving unsubstantiated election-fraud claims — with an unusually active run of enforced judicial and state pushback: a self-dealing IRS settlement voided, a 24-state grant-termination case won on final judgment, and a DOJ demand for Connecticut's voter rolls dismissed outright. None of this week's court losses for the administration were met with defiance or delay, which is the most important thing to watch in subsequent weeks. The clearest emerging risk driver is election administration: federal monitors are set to appear at New Hampshire polling places, and secretaries of state are treating federal cooperation as something to hedge against rather than rely on. Coming weeks will show whether judicial and state resistance keeps translating into enforced outcomes, or whether compliance with adverse rulings starts to erode.

weeks.relationship_note: Pressure rose this week mainly through the election-manipulation and judiciary-attacks indicators, driven by a Supreme Court emergency application over mail voting and a concrete impeachment threat against a sitting judge, but courts and states again produced real, evidence-based resistance that kept the Resilience Gap from widening further.

dri_gates_crossed.event: DOJ's emergency Supreme Court application (joined by 12 GOP-led states) to reinstate nationwide mail-voting restrictions before the midterms, reinforced by a D.C. Circuit ruling favoring the administration and continued unsubstantiated DHS noncitizen-voter claims.
dri_gates_crossed.why: For the first time, the mail-voting restriction dispute has reached the Supreme Court with an explicit request to allow implementation before the midterms, materially raising the near-term probability of restrictions taking effect nationwide; this is a qualitatively higher-stakes posture than ongoing lower-court litigation.

dri_gates_crossed.event: Rep. Andy Ogles announced concrete plans to file articles of impeachment against U.S. District Judge Allison Burroughs over a TPS ruling against the administration.
dri_gates_crossed.why: This moves from generalized baseline risk (rhetoric about judges) to an announced, specific legislative action targeting a named sitting judge for a particular ruling.

event_log.actor: Solicitor General John Sauer (DOJ), joined by 12 Republican-led states led by Missouri
event_log.target: Nationwide implementation of Trump's mail-in voting executive order (EO 14399) ahead of the midterms
event_log.action: Filed an emergency application asking the Supreme Court to lift the injunction blocking USPS and other federal agencies from implementing restrictions on mail-in voting before the November midterms.
event_log.notes: The Supreme Court requested a response by August 3, after the close of this reporting period; no decision has been issued yet. This is the first time the dispute has reached the Supreme Court with a request to allow implementation before the midterms.

event_log.actor: Three-judge panel, U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit
event_log.target: Plaintiffs challenging Trump's mail-in voting executive order (separate case track before Judge Carl Nichols)
event_log.action: Unanimously declined to block the executive order, upholding Judge Nichols's May ruling that a preliminary injunction was premature.
event_log.notes: A separate litigation track from the Talwani injunction now before the Supreme Court; this ruling addressed procedural prematurity, not the merits of the mail-voting restrictions.

event_log.actor: Election officials in California, Nevada, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania
event_log.target: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin's claim that the four states have 250,000+ noncitizens on their voter rolls
event_log.action: Publicly disputed DHS's uncorroborated noncitizen voter-roll figures; New Jersey disclosed its own review found 6,600 inadvertent noncitizen registrations (versus DHS's claimed 35,000 for that state), and DHS's own 'preliminary review' reportedly found only about 118,000 matches (versus the 250,000+ headline claim); states declined to hand over full voter files including Social Security numbers.
event_log.notes: DHS has not published its methodology. This also functions as continued narrative warfare (unsubstantiated claims of mass noncitizen voting) but is logged once, under Election manipulation, per protocol Section 4.2's instruction not to double-count a single event across indicators.

event_log.target: U.S. District Judge Allison Burroughs (D. Mass.)
event_log.action: Announced plans to file articles of impeachment against Judge Burroughs after she blocked the administration's termination of Temporary Protected Status for Somali nationals for a second time; allies characterized the ruling as defying the Supreme Court's June decision limiting judicial review of TPS determinations.
event_log.notes: Per protocol Section 5, the 'defiance of SCOTUS' framing is disputed, not established fact: Judge Burroughs's order reportedly rests on Fifth Amendment equal-protection and APA claims distinct from the TPS-designation-review question the Supreme Court addressed in its June ruling. Part of a broader pattern of GOP lawmakers threatening impeachment of judges who rule against the administration. Coverage of this specific announcement skews toward partisan/conservative outlets; treated as a confirmed fact of Ogles's announcement (multiple outlets agree), while the characterization of the ruling as 'defiance' is noted as contested.

event_log.target: Trump administration DHS termination of Temporary Protected Status for Somali nationals
event_log.action: Issued a fresh order blocking the administration from ending Somalia's TPS designation, based on Fifth Amendment equal-protection and Administrative Procedure Act claims.
event_log.notes: The court continued ruling against the administration on the merits notwithstanding public impeachment threats against the judge, evidence that judicial independence was not chilled by those threats this week.

weeks.trajectory_note: The Resilience Gap has held in the 'manageable strain' band for two consecutive tracked weeks (-5, then -8), but the composition of pressure shifted meaningfully this week: instead of diffuse pressure across many fronts, it concentrated in election administration, where the mail-voting dispute reached the Supreme Court with an explicit request to allow restrictions before the midterms, and in judiciary attacks, where a threat against judges moved from rhetoric to an announced, targeted impeachment effort. Both are indicators the protocol flags as carrying outsized structural weight — election manipulation is the highest-weighted DRI indicator, and judicial independence is the highest-weighted IRI indicator — so continued movement here would be the clearest signal of genuine backsliding rather than routine political conflict. The countervailing pattern remains intact: courts kept ruling against the administration without defiance, and states responded to unsubstantiated federal voter-roll claims with concrete counter-data rather than capitulation. The single most important thing to watch next is the Supreme Court's response to the mail-voting emergency application (due August 3, just after this window closes) — a stay favoring the administration ahead of the midterms would be a severe escalation, while a denial would reinforce this week's resistance pattern.
